rationale.complete: Round 1 done on 13 non-holdout periods in two channels: card and dated predictions, synthetic validation on 13 real schedules (6 worlds, 40 runs; estimator choice A1 fixed before data), post hoc burst worlds (A2), replication with per-unit fits and DL pooling, Brock-Durlauf fixed points with parametric P_multi and a multiplicity boundary gamma_c per period, 3 natives (G37 room replicas, G44 arms, G51 same-goal units), 179 estimate rows, frozen guarded confirm script (dry-run only).
rationale.faithfulness: HH283's core claim (multiple equilibria split same-type weeks) is not supported: no replica split, every period subcritical at its point estimate, fitted fields rank the order parameter. The share coefficient is real (validated against static fitness) but not identified as social coupling J because fast repo bursts reproduce it. P2, P3, P4 (by the letter), P6 and the G44 native failed. C = 1, D = 1, E = 0, F = 1, H = 1.
rationale.usefulness: Practical content is a negative with a bound: a week will not lock into a herd by chance at the observed fields, so operators should steer allocation through fields (owners, assignments, kickoff naming) rather than fear runaway herding. Habit (odds x12-400 of returning to one's own repo) is the largest term. The share coefficient itself is not actionable until J is identified.

one_line: Project choice has a share coefficient (+2 to +6 shared weeks, -12 private roles) that repo bursts mimic; no period is bistable and no same-field replica splits.
